title: Spec 8.2's actual floor metric is FAILING at 6.6 percent, and it was never the number being watched
description: Measured 2026-09-08: corroboration_by_outlet is 199/2999 = 6.6%, against spec 8.2's floor of 10%. The pre-registered gate would FAIL today. Every figure quoted during the bqa.18 investigation (16.8%, 17.1%, 20% per-pass) was score_match_rate_corroboration -- the OTHER 8.2 direction -- while the definition being quoted ('events carry assertions from 2 or more distinct outlets') is this one. Found only because a red-team review of the ranking spec flagged the conflation. The gap is itself diagnostic: match rate counts ANY second assertion, the floor counts only cross-outlet ones, so most matching that happens is same-outlet dedup rather than corroboration -- the easy case that recency ranking surfaced well, since one outlet's follow-up arrives minutes later.
design: Do NOT run the pre-registered gate until this has had a chance to move. It is one-shot: recording a FAIL on a system known to be mid-repair spends the pre-registration for nothing, and a threshold cannot honestly be re-run after looking. Ceiling arithmetic, both ends honest: merging the 64 cross-outlet pairs the probe detected gives 9.0%, still below the floor; extrapolating for a detector that keeps only 12% of true duplicates (~533 merges) gives ~30%. Ranking commit 51c850c targets exactly this population, since probable_misses requires different outlet_ids by construction. Watch corroboration_by_outlet after deploy, NOT the tally's match rate.
acceptance_criteria: corroboration_by_outlet is measured after the ranking change has run for a full window, and either clears 10% or the shortfall is attributed to a named cause rather than to an unmeasured one.

title: Integration tool schema requires 'standing' only, but _validate_item demands type + commitment_state
description: The 08:00 pass attributed 73 of 108 integration failures to validate:event_enums -- 26% of all material items, the single dominant defect class. Root cause is an asymmetry between _INTEGRATE_TOOL and _validate_item, not model disobedience. The event object in the tool schema declares required: ['standing'] (comprehend.py:888) while _validate_item rejects any NEW event whose type is not in _EVENT_TYPES or whose commitment_state is not in _COMMITMENT. A model omitting either field is following the schema exactly as published, and the whole ITEM is dropped for it. One JSON Schema object is being used for two different shapes: a candidate-matched event legitimately needs only candidate + standing (the _resolve_label branch short-circuits before the enum checks), while a NEW event needs summary + type + commitment_state + standing. required: ['standing'] is correct for the first shape and wrong for the second. The entity object has no required list at all, so validate:entity_fields carries the identical latent hazard. NOT YET CONFIRMED against a raw payload -- the structural asymmetry is established, but which field the model actually omits needs scripts/inspect_integration.py.
design: Open question, needs a decision: express the two shapes in the schema (oneOf / conditional required), or relax the validator. Forcing a commitment_state the model cannot determine writes junk into a KB whose quality the pre-registered gate measures, so this is not purely a schema fix. Either route changes what the model is asked and therefore wants an INTEGRATE_PROMPT_VERSION bump.
notes: URGENT because integrate_attempts is a one-way door that is NOT scoped to prompt version. gave_up_integration went 48 -> 65 in two hours; the same ~73 items sit at the front of every ORDER BY i.id pass and take a strike per hour for OUR defect. They die permanently at 3 regardless of any later fix. Mitigation before the fix ships: UPDATE item_triage SET integrate_attempts = 0 WHERE integrate_attempts > 0.
close_reason: Schema half shipped: anyOf branches on both the entity and event objects, so the published schema now asks for exactly what _validate_item demands. Validator half already shipped in 6baaf4c (commitment_state nullable) and 8c49c38 (missing/unknown failure keys). No INTEGRATE_PROMPT_VERSION bump -- see news-brief-ymk.

title: config.py is absent from the Dockerfile COPY list, so the image cannot import the supervisor
description: supervisor.py:25 and brief.py:40 import config at module level, but the Dockerfile COPY allowlist names 13 of 14 top-level modules and omits config.py. Reconstructing the image's file set and running 'import supervisor' fails with ModuleNotFoundError. docker-compose.yml:39 pulls ghcr.io/progdroid/news-brief:latest with no source mount, so the container's code IS the image's code. config.py is also missing from the workflow's paths: filter, so a commit touching only config.py triggers no build. Introduced when config-to-rows landed (1b5ba23, 3797ecf) without the three updates the dockerfile-copy-allowlist rule requires. Escapes local pytest and CI because both run on a full checkout. restart: no means the dead container stays quiet rather than crash-looping.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails when a module imported at top level by supervisor.py or brief.py is absent from the Dockerfile COPY list. Dockerfile and workflow paths both list config.py.
close_reason: Fixed in 51e72de. config.py added to the Dockerfile COPY list, the workflow paths filter and both ruff file lists. tests/test_packaging.py adds three graph-derived tests, each observed failing on config.py before its fix. Verified in the built image: pgdiag runs end to end, exit 0. Suite 1354 passed against postgres:18-alpine.

title: Four Google News proxies truncate at the 100-entry cap every poll
description: Measured 2026-09-08 over 4.3 days (scripts/measure_roll_off.py). Reuters Markets, Reuters World, Kyiv Independent and Yonhap all report entries_seen of EXACTLY 100 every poll, with reconstructed windows above it (151, 106, 130, 102) -- flicker 1.51/1.06/1.30/1.02. gnews median singles 0.062 against native 0.000. This is truncation INSIDE one poll, which spec section 3 names as the proxies' distinct loss mode, and NO poll interval fixes it: items leave by RANKING, not by ageing out. Reuters Markets sheds 185 items/day against a 100-item visible window. Remedy is a narrower query (shorter when:, deeper site: path) or a native feed -- but note the capture memory measured when:2d, when:7d and no-window ALL returning exactly 100, so narrowing must be MEASURED per feed rather than assumed to work.
acceptance_criteria: Each capping proxy either returns under 100 entries per poll, or is replaced by a native feed, or is documented as irreducible with the measured numbers behind that.

title: Diagnostic: is corroboration low from ranking, from the model, or because outlets do not overlap
description: events_matched/(matched+created) fell 26% (06:00) to 10.2% (13:00) against a pre-registered CORROBORATION_FLOOR of 0.10, and spec 8.2 makes that number the existence test for the event layer: 'below this the event layer bought essentially nothing over the claim ledger, which is the entire justification for 2.1'. candidate_events ranks by RECENCY (ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 30) over ANY single shared entity, so for a hub entity the 30 offered are arbitrary recent events and recall collapses precisely where cross-outlet overlap is most likely. candidate_cap_hit=60 against ~58 batches means essentially every batch truncates. Separately the gate applies a FIXED floor to a CUMULATIVE non-stationary quantity, which cannot be right at two corpus sizes.
design: Read-only, zero model calls. Discriminates THREE outcomes, not two: (A) the duplicate was offered and the model declined to match, (B) it existed but was never offered, (C) no duplicate existed and outlets genuinely do not overlap. C is untested and would invalidate the premise rather than the implementation. Calibrate the duplicate detector on the model's OWN matches (item pairs already sharing an event_id from different outlets) so the threshold is measured rather than invented -- without that positive control a null result is uninterpretable, because a similarity detector bounds duplicates from BELOW. Reconstruct retrievability generously, using the ideal entity set from event_entities and filtering events.created_at < the later event's creation, so a miss under ideal conditions is decisive. Report the CEILING: corroboration under the most favourable assignment of every probable miss -- if the ceiling still fails the floor, no retrieval work can rescue it.

title: An extraction with events but no entities dies as NoEntitySurvived and burns 3 attempts
description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-08 against a real payload. Items 76417 and 80775 logged NoEntitySurvived in the 08:00 pass; scripts/inspect_integration.py returns both as entities=[], events=[1] and _validate_item ACCEPTS them. write_extraction's empty branch requires BOTH lists empty, so an events-but-no-entities item skips it, enters the transaction, and hits 'if not entity_ids: raise NoEntitySurvived' with nothing having been refused. The comment above that branch asserts the distinction ('NOT the same as every entity was refused: that path went through resolution and had work rejected') but 'not entity_ids' is true in both cases -- a stated guarantee nothing enforces. Cost: the outcome is deterministic for the item at a given prompt version, so it fails identically every pass and dies at the 3-attempt ceiling, burning three 8192-token generations to reach a verdict available on the first. 5 items in the 08:00 tally.
design: Refusing is correct and should stay: candidate_events retrieves by entity id, so an entity-less event can never be offered as a candidate or matched, and would inflate events_created while never touching events_matched -- depressing the corroboration ratio the pre-registered gate reads, the same by-construction trap the occurred_at comment describes. What is wrong is refusing by raising and charging. Treat 'the model returned zero entities' like the empty-extraction branch: terminal, marked done, charged nothing, counted in its own tally field. Keep the raise for the genuine all-refused case, which did have work rejected and keeps its attempt.
close_reason: Fixed: entity-less extractions are terminal and uncharged; NoEntitySurvived keeps its attempt for the genuine all-refused case.

title: Populate Tally.failures so integration failures are self-attributing
description: Tally.failures is declared at comprehend.py:73 and written by nothing, so it always prints {} -- which reads as 'no failure details' rather than 'field nobody populates'. The 2026-09-08 pass reported failed_integration=72 of 259 material items (28%) with only ~21 attributable by reading tracebacks by hand (15 DNS, 6 savepoint), leaving ~51 with no attribution at all. That matters more than an aggregate suggests: a 28% rate against a 3-strike one-way door retires ~2% per sweep IF failures are independent, but a systematic class (e.g. 'no entity survived resolution') fails the same item every time and is at 100% risk, just three hours slower. The aggregate cannot separate unlucky from doomed.
acceptance_criteria: failures is keyed by cause and non-empty whenever failed_integration or deferred_transport is: _validate_item names which of its six return-None branches fired, write_extraction names its savepoint cause, and the batch path names transport vs the exception type.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: _is_transient splits no-verdict-obtained failures (connection, timeout, 429, 5xx) from item-attributable ones; transport failures count in deferred_transport and leave integrate_attempts alone. Tally.failures is populated by _validate_item (six branches), write_extraction (savepoint cause, NoEntitySurvived named), and the batch path. 1601 passed / 0 skipped with DATABASE_URL set; five mutations each caught by 3/3/10/1/2 tests. NOT yet deployed.

title: Transport failures must not charge the integrate_attempts ratchet
description: A DNS blip on 2026-09-08 06:01 failed three whole integration batches (COMPREHEND_INTEGRATE_BATCH=5, so ~15 items). comprehend.py:296's bare 'except Exception' charges +1 integrate_attempts to every item in the batch, but no model verdict was obtained -- the failure is a statement about the network, not about the item. integrate_attempts >= 3 is a one-way door, so three such blips retire an item permanently. Measured histogram after ~2 days: 48 items at 3 attempts (dead), 59 at 2, 264 at 1. Loss is biased toward the front of ORDER BY i.id, i.e. the oldest corpus.
acceptance_criteria: A ConnectionError, Timeout, 429 or 5xx leaves integrate_attempts unchanged and counts in a separate deferred_transport tally field; a 4xx other than 429, and any non-RequestException, still charge an attempt as before.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: _is_transient splits no-verdict-obtained failures (connection, timeout, 429, 5xx) from item-attributable ones; transport failures count in deferred_transport and leave integrate_attempts alone. Tally.failures is populated by _validate_item (six branches), write_extraction (savepoint cause, NoEntitySurvived named), and the batch path. 1601 passed / 0 skipped with DATABASE_URL set; five mutations each caught by 3/3/10/1/2 tests. NOT yet deployed.

title: bqa.4 cutover contract: obligations the KB schema places on the ledger migration
description: The 2026-09-02 KB schema spec places five separate obligations on bqa.4 that were scattered across four sections and never totalled. A second red-team pass found that missing one of them silently destroys the accountability record. Enumerated in spec section 6 'The cutover contract'. (1) Widen brief_memory._VALID_STATUS from {standing,challenged,broken} to the six-value set, and split the TTL and render predicates from '!= standing' to an explicit terminal-state set - otherwise _coerce_status returns None for confirmed/expired/withdrawn, they coerce to standing, the TTL filter deletes them after 7 days and select_working_set renders them as live fact. (2) Marshal first_seen, last_reaffirmed, resolution_date and resolved_on between the ledger's %Y-%m-%d strings and DATE columns, in BOTH directions. (3) Parse the c-0001 id format for the ledger_id backfill. (4) Backfill extractor_model and prompt_version, which ship nullable only to accommodate pre-existing rows. (5) Enforce the one-entity-per-company extraction rule, which no unique key can express.
acceptance_criteria: A round-trip test: every value the claims.status CHECK permits survives _coerce_status without degrading. Write-direction coverage alone is insufficient - that is the probe measuring the wrong layer.
notes: Item 1 DISCHARGED 2026-09-02 in b097a77, ahead of bqa.4 rather than inside it. _VALID_STATUS widened to six; _TERMINAL_STATUS (= the claims_freeze_claim_text tuple) and _TTL_EXEMPT_STATUS (= the six minus standing) replace the two '!= standing' predicates; _apply_status refuses a transition off a terminal status. Strict xfail removed; its hardcoded enum replaced by pg_constraint parsing plus a new set-equality test proving the CHECK equals _VALID_STATUS in BOTH directions (positive control: a 7th value in _VALID_STATUS fails only the new test, not the coercion one). 1313 passed, 0 skipped, 0 xfailed against postgres:18-alpine. STILL OPEN: items 2-5 (date marshalling both directions, c-0001 ledger_id parsing, extractor_model/prompt_version backfill, one-entity-per-company) - each constrains a migration bqa.4 has not written yet.
close_reason: All five obligations verified discharged across three commits: item 1 in b097a77 (noted 2026-09-02); items 2-4 (date marshalling both directions, c-0001 ledger_id parsing, extractor_model/prompt_version backfill) in bqa.10; item 5 (one-entity-per-company) in bqa.4b at comprehend.py:889, where _resolve_entity refuses an instrument entity whose symbol a company already maps, enforced in SQL rather than in the prompt per the jx9.5 lesson. Acceptance criterion met in BOTH directions by tests/test_kb_schema.py:973, which asserts set equality between the live pg_constraint values and brief_memory._VALID_STATUS rather than a hardcoded list; tests/test_comprehend_integration.py:524 pins item 5. No code left to write.

title: An unmarked rewrite is a contradiction, not a refinement
description:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-31 after three break runs under prompt v4. The original framing - recall fell, so reword the restatement guard - is WRONG and is superseded by what the runs actually show.

THE DEFECT. The model is not failing to detect contradictions. It detects them and ABSORBS them into the claim text, echoing the id and leaving status=standing. Of the true breaks scored standing: 6 of 6 in run A, 3 of 3 in runs B and C had their claim text rewritten to the corrected version. gs-08 stored as Portugal tops group with 4 pts came back as Portugal and Colombia are tied at 4 pts, standing. gs-09 stored as Colombia holds 6 pts came back as both teams hold 4 pts, standing. gs-10 stored as Tehran intends to resume collecting Hormuz fees came back as the toll is being replaced by Gulf investment deals, standing.

THIS IS A HOLE IN jx9.5. That issue froze claim text once status is not standing, to stop the replay Patriot bug. But the freeze is conditioned on a field the MODEL controls: keep status=standing and the rewrite passes as a refinement, which the prompt explicitly permits (you may reword its claim if today refined it).

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not what this issue used to say. The old description said a lost break leaves a false claim standing. It does not - the ledger content quietly self-corrects, so the reader is never told the false fact. What is destroyed is the ACCOUNTABILITY RECORD: no trace survives that the claim was ever wrong. A ledger that silently edits its own history cannot answer how often were we wrong, which is the measurement Epic 1 exists to produce. Spec 3.3: the original claim is precisely what accountability is measured against, it is what the reader was told.

THE SIGNAL IS DETERMINISTIC. Reusing _claim_fingerprint, numeric tokens the stored claim asserted and the rewrite DROPPED separate the classes cleanly. On run A standing rows, restricted to admissible claims, it fires on exactly gs-08, gs-09, gs-10, gs-16 - all four true breaks - and on nothing else. The other rows it fires on (gs-03, gs-12, gs-13, gs-21) are all inadmissible and no longer reach this path now that 93u landed. DROPPED, not merely changed: adding a number (BOJ raised the rate to 1.0 percent ON JUNE 16) is genuine refinement and must not trip it.

THE FIX, decided with the user 2026-08-31. In merge_ledger, when an echoed id arrives with status=standing and the rewrite drops a number the stored claim asserted: keep the ORIGINAL text, force status=challenged, and record the attempted rewrite as the evidence the way broken_by already works. challenged rather than broken because a dropped number can be innocent compression, and because challenged is still quarantined (read by nothing), so a false fire costs nothing today - which makes this the cheapest possible moment to turn it on.

NOT IN SCOPE: rewording the restatement guard. gs-08/gs-09/gs-10 are numeric and standings negations; the restatement guard never touched them. Evidence: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md and the three run artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. DONE. merge_ledger keeps the ORIGINAL claim text when an echoed standing row arrives with a rewrite that drops a number the stored claim asserted, marks it challenged, and records the attempted rewrite in broken_by.
2. DONE. A refinement that only ADDS numbers or detail still reaffirms and may still reword; test_a_standing_claim_can_still_be_refined stays green.
3. AMENDED 2026-08-31, and the amendment is the honest part. As written this asked to recover gs-08 and gs-09 without precision below 75 percent. The approved design CANNOT move that number: the guard records challenged, the gold set positive class is broken, so those rows stay false negatives by construction. The criterion was written before the enforcement verdict was chosen and should have been caught then. Replaced by: the guard DETECTS and RECORDS gs-08 and gs-09 rather than letting them be silently rewritten. Met - gs-08 caught 2/2 runs, gs-09 1/2, precision held at 75 and 100 percent.
4. DONE. Measured over two runs: guard fired 7/23 and 5/23; on admissible rows it fired only on true breaks, with ZERO false fires (0 of 17, both runs). Every false fire sat on an inadmissible row that the 93u admission guard now rejects upstream.
notes: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-31 under prompt v4 (93u shipped the kind rubric + admission guard). Three break runs, not one: precision is now 100% and STABLE (v3 was 75%; the surviving false positive gs-21 is rejected upstream by the admission guard). Recall did not simply fall, its composition changed. gs-16 - the row this issue names as must-recover - is now caught 2/3 runs after being LOST at v3. gs-09 and gs-10 moved the other way. Per-row over 3 runs: gs-04 3/3, gs-16 2/3, gs-08 0/3, gs-09 0/3, gs-10 0/3, gs-14 0/3, gs-15 0/3. THE DENOMINATOR CHANGED: gs-14 and gs-15 are inadmissible and now disappear upstream exactly as predicted, so they can no longer be scored as lost breaks; the real denominator is the 5 admissible true breaks. WHAT REMAINS: gs-08, gs-09, gs-10 are missed outright (not near the boundary) and share a shape - numeric and standings negations ('tops group with 4 pts' vs 'both tied on 4 pts'), which the restatement guard never touches. That is a DIFFERENT fix from rewording the restatement guard. Full write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md
close_reason: Built and measured. The fix is in _reaffirm: an echoed standing claim whose rewrite DROPS a number the stored claim asserted keeps its original text, is forced to challenged, and records the attempted rewrite as evidence. Dropped and not merely changed, so adding a date or detail still rewords normally. Reuses _claim_fingerprint. Also fixed the instrument: the break probe read status straight off the model reply and never called merge_ledger, so the guard was invisible there; probe now reports ledger_status and guard_fired alongside an unchanged predicted, keeping earlier runs comparable. Two runs: fired 7/23 and 5/23, and on ADMISSIBLE rows it fired only on true breaks with zero false fires (0 of 17 both runs) - every false fire sat on an inadmissible row that 93u now rejects upstream. gs-08 caught 2/2, gs-09 1/2. Known gap, stated not solved: a purely qualitative reversal that drops no number passes untouched; it is not measurable on this fixture because every persistent miss there was numeric. jx9.6 must re-check the fire rate before lifting the challenged quarantine, since a false fire is free only while challenged is read by nothing. Suite 934 -> 938. Write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md

title: Add claim status lifecycle: standing/challenged/broken + broke_on + broken_by
description: Spec 12.3 fix #3, and the ONLY one of the three load-bearing fixes with no bd issue (found 2026-08-29 by mapping the 12.3 table onto bd). Add status in {standing, challenged, broken}, broke_on (date) and broken_by (claim id or event ref) to ledger claims, and instruct reconcile to mark contradictions rather than silently rewriting the claim. This IS propagation rule 1 - the rule the 90-brief replay was run to validate (70 resolutions, ~0.27 breaks/brief, ~61% precision). Prerequisite for news-brief-jx9.5 (immutable once status != standing) and news-brief-jx9.6 (exempt non-standing from TTL and cap), both of which currently presuppose a field that does not exist. Steal gbrain's resolution vocabulary per spec section 10.
design: Vocabulary from gbrain takes: correct/incorrect/partial/unresolvable + superseded_by, narrowed to standing/challenged/broken for v1. Status must be specified to the 'status field' standard in spec 12.2: explicit per-value rules, a stated default (standing), and an explicit negative case ('absence is not contradiction'; 'a restatement, escalation or confirmation is not a break').
acceptance_criteria: merge_ledger preserves status/broke_on/broken_by across reconcile; a claim marked broken keeps its original text; default is standing when the model omits the field; reconcile prompt states the negative cases; tests cover each transition.
close_reason: status/broke_on/broken_by land on every row, QUARANTINED per the agreed decision: rendering, TTL retirement and working-set ordering all ignore the field, pinned by two quarantine tests. broke_on is stamped on the first transition out of standing and never rewritten. Prompt specifies the field to the spec 12.2 standard (per-value rules, stated default, both negative cases). BOUNDARY: the prompt asks the model not to reword a broken claim, but merge does not yet ENFORCE immutability - that is news-brief-jx9.5, now unblocked. Reconcile output measured at ~2970 worst-case tokens vs the 4096 budget.

title: Build the gold-set regression harness for break detection
description: Seed from the 24 hand-audited break detections in the 2026-08-29 replay. Target: precision >=85%, baseline 61%. A run that improves recall while dropping precision below baseline is a regression. Must also check every enum field for VARIANCE, not just presence - severity currently returns high on 25/25 live claims.
notes: DONE 2026-08-29. Built: tests/fixtures/gold_set_breaks.json (23 labelled items, committed), scripts/score_gold_set.py (manual scorer, live Haiku, one call per item), tests/test_gold_set.py (26 offline tests: fixture schema + scorer arithmetic; CI has no API key so the scoring run never fires there). Suite 792 -> 884, ruff clean. FIRST RUN: precision 75.0% vs a 33.3% baseline, recall 42.9% vs 100%, 13 false positives converted, 4 true breaks LOST -> filed as jx9.9. Admissible rows only: precision 100%, recall 60%, zero false positives. Fixture decisions: 3-valued labels with unclear excluded from the denominator; admissible flag marks the 6 ephemeral-price rows the 93u admission guard must reject upstream; seed row r-0808 withheld because it carries Bigdata.com-derived numeric values and this repo is public. The spec's ~61% baseline is NOT reproducible - it was eyeballed off audit.py output that prints claim[:105] of a field replay.py had already truncated to 150 chars; the fixture is the baseline of record. Write-up: docs/2026-08-29-gold-set-first-run.md.
close_reason: Gold set built, committed and run; results in docs/2026-08-29-gold-set-first-run.md. Unblocks 93u.

title: Add horizon_days and resolution_date; exempt non-standing claims from TTL and cap
description: horizon_elapsed at resolution is the calibration datapoint ('broken at 2 days against 180' vs just 'broken'). The TTL exemption is correct and cheap but secondary - the replay shows the cap, not the TTL, is what loses claims.
notes: STILL blocked by decision after the first gold-set run (2026-08-29, jx9.7). The run does NOT license lifting write-then-quarantine: status does show real variance (standing 16 / broken 5 / challenged 2 across 23 probes), but its recall collapsed to 42.9% - 4 of 7 true breaks missed, filed as jx9.9. Making status act on retention now would let a wrong verdict change what the ledger keeps, which spec 6.1 classes as a permanent integration error. Lift this only after jx9.9 restores recall AND a re-score holds precision. See docs/2026-08-29-gold-set-first-run.md.
close_reason: Built and measured. Three parts. (1) TTL exemption for both non-standing statuses - a broken claim is the accountability record, a challenged one is still resolving; standing claims still age out. (2) The working set SPLITS them, deliberately against spec 12.3 fix #11's one-line 'exempt from TTL and cap': taken literally that pins broken rows into the 25-row window that is sent to the model and rendered to the reader, and crowding-out is this system's measured primary failure. So broken LEAVES the window (stays in storage for measurement; rendering it as background states a fact the ledger knows false) and challenged RANKS FIRST so it is never evicted, implemented as priority not extra slots because the cap is a prompt budget. Challenged renders with an (in doubt) cue. (3) horizon_days / resolution_date / horizon_elapsed, shipped WRITE-THEN-QUARANTINE. THE GATE WAS ANSWERED AGAINST ITS OWN WORDING, explicitly: recall was NOT restored (14-57 percent over 8 runs, no trend). What justified lifting is that on ADMISSIBLE rows only - the population production can store now that 93u exists - precision was 100 percent with ZERO false positives in all 8 runs; every false positive in the all-rows column sat on an inadmissible row that the admission guard rejects upstream. Low recall makes the lift safer, not riskier: fewer rows are affected and the affected ones have never been wrong. horizon_days survived its first measurement non-degenerate (4 distinct values, modal 7 rather than the stated default 30) - the first new field in this epic to do so. PROMPT_VERSION 4 -> 5. Suite 938 -> 963. Consequence filed as news-brief-6wc (storage now unbounded in time for non-standing rows). First change in Epic 1 that alters brief output. Write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md

title: Make claim text immutable once status is not standing
description: The replay marked the Patriot claim broken AND rewrote its text into a description of the reversal, so the ledger reads as though the reversal was reversed. The original assertion is what accountability is measured against. Rewording is correct for refining a standing claim, wrong for a break; the reversal goes in broken_by.
close_reason: _reaffirm updates claim text only while the claim is standing AND stays standing, so the freeze covers the very reply that breaks it - the measured Patriot failure. broken_by still records the reversal. Refining a standing claim still works (regression test). The pon dedup path folds through the same _reaffirm, so it is covered rather than being a back door.

title: Record extractor_model and prompt_version on every row
description: Hard precondition before any DDL. The model is configuration, integration errors are permanent, and nothing currently ties a row to its extractor. Precedent: the Sonnet 4.6->5 swap silently changed thinking behaviour and inflated tokens ~30%, truncating signals with no error raised. Spec section 12.2.
close_reason: merge_ledger stamps extractor_model + prompt_version on every write via injectable kwargs; provenance tracks the latest write and is outside the jx9.5 text freeze. PROMPT_VERSION=1 with a bump note on the template. Untouched rows keep their own provenance (guard test).

title: Add origin: extracted vs authored to claims
description: Source-grounded rows (extracted) are the only ones a propagation rule, thesis or calibration aggregate may read. Brief-authored interpretation is persisted and scorable but may never support a claim or be rendered back as established fact. One column; replaces the withdrawn read-only-renderer rule. Spec section 4.1.
close_reason: origin extracted|authored on every row, default extracted, reaffirm may promote authored->extracted. Prompt specifies it with per-value rules, worked examples spanning the range, and a stated default. READ SIDE QUARANTINED: the 4.1 render filter is not wired until the gold set shows the field has variance - same reasoning as status, reinforced by 47q. PROMPT_VERSION bumped 1->2.

title: Rewrite the ESTABLISHED block and add a driver field
description: brief_memory.py:200 emits '## ESTABLISHED - THE READER ALREADY KNOWS THESE' plus 'Do NOT re-explain'. The model adopted the heading as vocabulary and ships literal (established) tags meaning 'I know this and am not telling you'. Rewrite the header/instruction, and add a driver field plus explicit permission to restate a driver when explaining a market move.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add restatement guard and claim-admission guard to reconcile
description: Replay measured ~61% precision on 24 'broken' detections. Every audited false positive is a restatement/confirmation misread as contradiction (e.g. 'BOJ raised policy rate to 1.0%' broken by 'BOJ rate decision executed at 1.0%, not just expected'). Add the explicit rule that a restatement, escalation or confirmation is NOT a break - the mirror guard ('absence is not contradiction') already works. Separately, enforce at merge time that ephemeral price levels are not admitted as durable claims; the prompt already forbids it and it happens anyway. The 24 audited detections are the regression set.
notes: SCOPE NARROWED (2026-08-29, jx9.7 session): fix #4 (the restatement guard) is ALREADY LIVE. It shipped inside jx9.8 as part of commit 22a9776 — brief_memory._RECONCILE_TEMPLATE now carries 'A restatement, escalation or confirmation is not a break, however much more strongly it is worded', with the BOJ 1.0% example from the audit as its worked case. The 61%-precision baseline was measured against replay.py's TEMPLATE, which had only the absence guard. So what remains under 93u is (a) MEASURE the shipped guard with scripts/score_gold_set.py before writing any more prompt, and (b) the claim-admission guard, which is genuinely not built: 6 of the 23 gold-set rows are marked admissible=false (ephemeral price levels stored as durable claims) and that is merge_ledger-side enforcement, not prompt wording.

(b) The claim-admission guard is BUILT and MEASURED: kind=claim|observation on reconcile replies with a rubric written to the status standard, enforced as a hard drop in merge_ledger on NEW rows only (echoed ids and dedup matches are reaffirmation, exempt per jx9.5), failing open on a missing label with kind as a scorer variance field so absence is loud. prompt_version 3 -> 4. Result: 0 of 17 admissible claims lost, 0 price prints entered the ledger across all 23 items, kind variance claim 18 / observation 5. The model SPLITS a price-anchored claim rather than dropping it - level as observation, durable half as claim - and on gs-03 the surviving half converges on almost exactly gs-16, the row hand-labelled admissible. Write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md

title: Diagnostic: inspect one real integration call and its per-row verdicts
description:
comprehend gives no way to ask WHY integration rejected an item. Tally.failures is declared (comprehend.py:68) and written by NOTHING - grep for "failures[" and ".failures" both return zero hits - so it always prints as {}, which reads like "no failure details" rather than "field nobody populates". failed_integration is a bare count with no attribution. That is fail-closed-needs-status-not-count: a multi-gate silent path returning a number nobody can act on.

This bit on 2026-09-07: the first live comprehend pass returned Tally(items_seen=300, material=159, sampled=20, failed_integration=172, empty_extraction=7, assertions_written=0). Every eligible item failed (172 + 7 = 179 = 159 + 20), every integration call came back stop_reason=tool_use with healthy output tokens, and nothing in the logs could say which of _validate_item s six return-None branches fired.

scripts/inspect_integration.py fills the gap: it rebuilds ONE integration call exactly as comprehend.run() builds it, dumps the raw emit_extraction payload, and prints _validate_item s verdict per row. Read-only - it SELECTs, calls the model once, prints, and rolls back, so no item_triage counter moves and no integration attempt is burned.
design:
Mirror run() s integration path rather than approximating it, or the probe measures a different layer than the one that failed:
- the SAME select (verdict=material, integrate_attempts < 3, integrated_at IS NULL OR integrate_prompt_version < N, ORDER BY i.id) so it probes the exact front-of-queue rows that failed
- the SAME candidate assembly: SurfaceIndex.build, index.match over cleaned title+body, entity ids ranked DESC and capped at CANDIDATE_ENTITY_CAP, candidate_events()
- build_integration_request() and call_integration() themselves, not a hand-rolled request

Deliberately NOT included: a mirror of _validate_item that explains WHICH branch rejected a row. A hand-written copy agrees with itself by construction and cannot detect its own drift from the function it claims to explain. The raw payload is the evidence; a human or an agent reads it against the four enum sets. _validate_item stays authoritative for accept/reject.

Batch size from argv[1], defaulting to 5.

Runs in-container, since there is no checkout on the deploy host:
  docker compose run --rm --entrypoint python newsbrief scripts/inspect_integration.py

CI needs no change: docker-publish.yml lints scripts as a DIRECTORY (not a file list) and scripts/** is already in the rebuild trigger paths. tests/test_packaging.py does not reference scripts - verified with a positive control, 281 lines and 14 Dockerfile/COPY references, so the empty grep is a real negative.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/inspect_integration.py exists, passes ruff check and ruff format --check, and the suite still passes. Run against production it prints the offered item/entity/event candidate ids, the response envelope (stop_reason and usage), the raw emit_extraction payload as indented JSON, and one ACCEPT/REJECT line per returned row with entity and event counts. It writes nothing: verify by EFFECT that item_triage.integrate_attempts is unchanged across a run.
close_reason: Built and committed in d48b036 (scripts/inspect_integration.py); the commit named the bead but nothing closed it. Read-only probe: same select, same candidate assembly, same request builder as run(), dumps the raw emit_extraction payload and prints _validate_item's verdict per row, then rolls back.

title: Warn at boot when a KNOBS env var is set but no settings row backs it
description:
A knob set in the environment on an established host is SILENTLY ignored. config.knob() (config.py:207) resolves from a settings row or the code default and never falls back to the environment at read time, and config.import_settings_from_env() (config.py:222) copies env into settings ONLY while the global settings table is empty. On any host past first boot, editing docker-compose.yml or .env and restarting therefore changes nothing, logs nothing, and errors nothing.

This is not hypothetical. On 2026-09-07 COMPREHEND_ENABLED=1 was set in the host compose and the stack restarted; the container carried the variable, no row existed, and the 19:00 comprehend pass logged "disabled by COMPREHEND_ENABLED; nothing read". It cost a rollout window and was only caught because the acceptance criteria for news-brief-bqa.11 demanded verification by EFFECT rather than by reading the config back. The behaviour is deliberate and correct - see the knob() docstring, which explains why a read-time env fallback would be worse - so this issue is about making the no-op VISIBLE, not about changing resolution.

The trap generalises to every knob and every future flag flip on this host, which is why it is worth a boot-time check rather than a note in a runbook.
design:
Emit a warning at startup, next to the import_settings_from_env call so it fires whether or not the import ran, for every KNOBS entry where the environment is set and the settings row does not back it.

Predicate, which must match what the CONSUMER reads (a guard must test the exact predicate its consumer reads):
  key = spec.key(name)   -- NOT name. Knob.key() returns self.env or name, so
                            MODEL keys on NEWSBRIEF_MODEL while COMPREHEND_ENABLED
                            keys on its bare name. Using the attribute name would
                            reproduce the very mismatch this is meant to catch.
  raw = os.environ.get(key)
  warn when raw is not None and raw.strip() and (no row for key, OR row value != raw.strip())

Both arms matter. The absent-row arm is the case that fired on 2026-09-07. The disagreeing-value arm is the more insidious one: an operator edits compose, restarts, and a row set months ago silently wins - identical symptom, and nothing in the logs distinguishes them.

Empty values MUST NOT warn. The repo anchor declares all seven COMPREHEND_* vars as ${VAR:-}, so six of them resolve to empty strings on every boot; warning on those makes the check noise and it will be ignored within a week. This matches the importer, which already skips on "raw is None or not raw.strip()".

The message should name the key, the ignored environment value, the effective value, and the remedy (write the settings row), so it is actionable without a code read.
acceptance_criteria:
A boot-time check logs one warning per KNOBS key whose environment value is set and non-empty while no settings row backs it, or while the row disagrees with it. Message names the key, the ignored env value, the effective value, and the fix.

Tests, in tests/test_config.py alongside the existing knob tests:
- absence case: env var set, no row -> warning fires, naming that key
- disagreement case: env var set, row set to a different value -> warning fires
- PRESENCE SIBLING (required, not optional): env var set, row set to the SAME value -> NO warning. An absence-assertion without a presence-sibling passes just as well against a check that never runs at all.
- empty case: env var set to the empty string, no row -> NO warning
- key derivation: a knob WITH env= (MODEL) is checked under NEWSBRIEF_MODEL, and a knob WITHOUT env= (COMPREHEND_ENABLED) under its bare name

Mentally delete the check and confirm each test above fails. Verify the real thing by EFFECT on the host: set a knob in the environment with no row, restart, and find the warning in the startup log.
close_reason: Detector + boot warning + once-per-episode Telegram alert, pushed in 1131d2c. Verified by mutation: gutting the detector fails 11 of 12 tests, a constant episode key fails exactly 1.

title: Enable COMPREHEND_ENABLED in production and run the pre-registered gate
description: bqa.4b is built, pushed and disabled. Nothing fills the KB until COMPREHEND_ENABLED is flipped on the host, and the pre-registered gate in scripts/score_comprehension.py has never run against real data. This is the load-bearing next step for Epic 3: bqa.5 (propagation rules) and bqa.6 (review queue) both act on a KB that is currently static, and news-brief-115 waits explicitly on the gate having been run. Blocked on nothing in code as of 2026-09-07: the two gate-validity bugs (wvt, uer) are fixed and pushed.
design: DESIGNED SO FAR, 2026-09-07 (brainstorm only, no rollout plan written yet). Sequencing was decided: fix gate-distorting bugs BEFORE flipping, because the gate is a one-shot instrument whose thresholds may not be retuned after it has run (the script says so at line 31). wvt and uer are done. 3wb stays deferred (unreachable while INTEGRATE_PROMPT_VERSION is 1) and ya4 stays deferred deliberately, so the gate measures the system it was registered against. STILL OPEN AND NEEDS THE USER: (1) how many items a day is capture actually producing? This sets both cost exposure and the accumulation window, and cannot be answered from the dev repo - it needs a count off the host. (2) Does triage run on a cheaper model? TRIAGE_MODEL and INTEGRATE_MODEL are knobs defaulting to follow MODEL (claude-sonnet-5); triage is the volume lever at COMPREHEND_MAX_ITEMS=300 per hourly pass. (3) How long to accumulate before running the gate. The gate needs an outlet with 10+ assertions, 2+ distinct enum values at 10 percent each, and multi-outlet corroboration between 10 and 60 percent, so it needs volume AND elapsed time. Consider a cheap smoke pass first (low MAX_ITEMS) to prove the pipeline writes rows in production, kept separate from the measurement window.
acceptance_criteria: COMPREHEND_ENABLED is on for the host and the settings row is verified by EFFECT (rows appearing in item_triage, entities, events, assertions), never by reading the row back. A stated accumulation window has elapsed. scripts/score_comprehension.py has been run from a checkout against production and its output recorded verbatim in the repo, PASS or FAIL, with the thresholds untouched. If it FAILS, the failure is attributable to a named cause rather than to the plumbing.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-09-07. The previous NOTES said scripts/ is NOT in the Dockerfile COPY and the gate must run from a checkout. That was WRONG, and it was a metadata-is-not-state error: it read news-brief-115 (which exists to REMOVE the line) as evidence the line was absent.

scripts/ IS in the COPY allowlist, at Dockerfile:55, added 2026-09-05 specifically so the gate can run in-container. The command is in the Dockerfile comment and in 115:

  docker compose run --rm --entrypoint python newsbrief scripts/score_comprehension.py

--entrypoint python is required; ENTRYPOINT is [python, brief.py] and takes a MODE, so without it the script path is parsed as a mode. Exit codes: 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 no database configured. Redirect to a file rather than piping to tee, which would eat the status.

The checkout route is not merely unnecessary, it does not work as-is: docker-compose.yml has NO ports: key anywhere, so Postgres is on the compose network only and is unreachable from a host shell. The host compose may differ; the in-container route does not care either way.

PLUMBING REHEARSAL DONE 2026-09-07, before the flag flip: the gate ran end to end against the empty KB and returned clean negatives on every check (no rows / no events / no assertions, and not yet measurable for the per-outlet standing check). Every query plans and executes. This is what rules out an F6-style UndefinedColumn burning a real measurement window.

=== FLAG FLIP: FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED SILENTLY, 2026-09-07 ===

The compose file was edited to set COMPREHEND_ENABLED=1 and the stack restarted at 18:16. The 19:00 pass then logged: Comprehend: disabled by COMPREHEND_ENABLED; nothing read. Nothing ran; zero triage rows, zero attempts burned, backlog intact.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by probe not by inference. config.knob() (config.py:207) resolves a knob from a settings ROW or the code default and NEVER falls back to the environment at read time; its docstring says so explicitly. config.import_settings_from_env (config.py:222) copies env into settings ONLY when the global settings table is empty. Probe results: 11 global rows (so the importer no-ops), no COMPREHEND_ENABLED row, and COMPREHEND_ENABLED=1 present in the container environment. This is env-var-needs-compose-passthrough firing exactly as that memory describes.

THE SETTINGS KEY IS THE BARE NAME. Knob.key() returns self.env or name, and common.py:265 declares Knob(bool, False) with NO env= kwarg, so the row key is COMPREHEND_ENABLED, NOT NEWSBRIEF_COMPREHEND_ENABLED. Contrast MODEL, which stores under NEWSBRIEF_MODEL. A row under the prefixed name is ignored with no warning.

Ruled out during the investigation, so nobody re-checks them: cache staleness (60s TTL had 44 minutes to expire, and comprehend runs as a FRESH CHILD PROCESS each pass so its cache starts empty), and value casing (coerce_knob does text.lower() in _TRUTHY, so True/TRUE/on/yes/1 all work; t and enabled do not).

FIX APPLIED 2026-09-07, one row, no redeploy and no restart:
  INSERT INTO settings (key, user_id, value) VALUES (COMPREHEND_ENABLED, NULL, 1)
  ON CONFLICT (key) WHERE user_id IS NULL DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value, updated_at = now();
The WHERE user_id IS NULL in the conflict clause is REQUIRED: settings_key_global (migrations/0001:23) is a PARTIAL unique index and Postgres needs the predicate to infer it.

The compose line stays. It is what seeds the row on a fresh database, and tests/test_packaging.py enforces anchor-to-KNOBS parity. Compose is right for a NEW deployment; the row is the only path on an ESTABLISHED one. Minor drift, no action: the repo anchor declares all seven COMPREHEND_* vars (docker-compose.yml:149-155) but the host container env carries only COMPREHEND_ENABLED.

=== LIVE RISK WHILE THE BACKLOG DRAINS ===

integrate_attempts >= 3 is a ONE-WAY DOOR and is NOT scoped to the prompt version: once an item hits 3, no INTEGRATE_PROMPT_VERSION bump brings it back. Both failure paths increment it (whole-batch exception, and the dropped path where _validate_item rejected a returned row). The integration SELECT is ORDER BY i.id LIMIT 300, so the SAME low-id items sit at the front of every pass and a systematic failure retires them at one attempt per hour. Recoverable only by hand, and only if noticed: UPDATE item_triage SET integrate_attempts = 0 WHERE ... There is no alerting path.

STOP-LOSS, pre-registered: if integrate_attempts >= 3 climbs while assertions stays at or near zero, set the COMPREHEND_ENABLED row back to 0 before the next hourly pass and diagnose from the logs.

PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATIONS for the first real pass (written before looking): item_triage rows = 300 or fewer if DEADLINE_SECONDS 2400 bit mid-integration; reason=tracked_entity 0 (entities starts empty); reason=tracked_story 0 (nothing writes stories); reason=tracked_claim small, seeded from claims; reason=sampled up to 20; assertions > 0 if integration works at all; integrate_attempts >= 3 EXACTLY 0, which is arithmetically forced after one pass.

=== MEASURED CONTEXT ===

Volume off the host 2026-09-07: steady state 700-900 new items/day across 24 outlets (2026-09-04 s 1926 is a first-fill artifact, do not use it in a rate). Comprehend runs hourly, so about 30 items/pass in steady state and MAX_ITEMS=300 never binds once the backlog drains. Standing backlog at flip was roughly 4100 untriaged items, about 14 passes to drain. Only about 25 percent of items carry 150+ chars of body, so the 12.3 depth-tier split is load-bearing.

MODEL DECISION 2026-09-07: TRIAGE_MODEL and INTEGRATE_MODEL stay EMPTY, both following MODEL=claude-sonnet-5, for the whole measurement window. Triage costs roughly 0.20 USD/day and Haiku 4.5 would save about half of that, but item_triage.triage_model is stored PER ROW, so a mid-window swap blends two populations in a gate that has no arm to separate them. Revisit as a pure cost question AFTER the gate, using real durations and token counts from comprehend._timed_post.

STILL OPEN: the accumulation window length, to be sized against the real material rate from the first healthy pass. The gate needs an outlet at 10+ assertions, two enum values at 10 percent each, and multi-outlet corroboration between 10 and 60 percent, which needs elapsed calendar time and not just volume.

title: Integration calls reuse a timeout sized for the signals call
description:
comprehend.call_integration goes through brief._post_messages, which takes only a payload and hardcodes SIGNALS_TIMEOUT=90 with SIGNALS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2. Those values were sized for extract_signals, and brief.py:2852 states the reason inline: 'generous: extraction runs AFTER delivery, so latency is free'.

That justification does NOT transfer. comprehend runs as an hourly job with its own DEADLINE_SECONDS, and integration generates at INTEGRATE_MAX_TOKENS=8192 -- a far heavier generation than the signals call. Two coupled risks: (1) 90s may be too short for an 8192-token tool-use generation, in which case items land in failed_integration, integrate_attempts climbs to its ceiling of 3, and the item is abandoned -- counted, but wrong, and it reads as a model failure rather than a timeout; (2) two attempts at 90s is up to 180s of wall clock per batch charged against comprehend's own deadline, so a slow API shrinks how much of a pass completes.

This repo has already paid for exactly this once: signals used timeout=30 copied from a Haiku call, which was too short for Sonnet and wiped the day's signals (regression fixed in e255436). The recorded lesson is to match a post-generation call's timeout to its model AND its workload.
design:
Not fixed inside the bqa.4b build for two reasons. It touches brief.py's shared HTTP path and changes a function signature used by the delivered brief, which is a wider blast radius than a wiring task should take. And the right timeout for an 8192-token integration generation is UNMEASURED -- picking one now would be inventing an unmeasured constant, which is the thing this project's quarantine rule exists to prevent.

Likely shape: give _post_messages optional timeout and attempts parameters defaulting to the current SIGNALS_* values so the brief path is unchanged, then have comprehend pass its own. Size them from measurement once comprehend has run in production and job_runs shows real integration latency.
acceptance_criteria: _post_messages accepts a caller-supplied timeout and attempt count, the signals path keeps its current values unchanged, comprehend passes values derived from observed integration latency, and the chosen numbers are justified against measured data rather than assumed.
close_reason: Fixed together (they both distort what the pre-registered comprehension gate measures). wvt: brief._post_messages gains keyword timeout/max_attempts defaulting to the signals budget, so that caller is provably unchanged (two positive-control tests). comprehend routes through a new _timed_post that logs each call's elapsed seconds, and sizes itself via two new settings knobs, COMPREHEND_INTEGRATE_TIMEOUT=300 and COMPREHEND_TRIAGE_TIMEOUT=90, plus compose anchors. Integration now makes ONE HTTP attempt: item_triage.integrate_attempts < 3 already retries across hourly passes, so a second HTTP attempt multiplied against it (up to 6 charged 8192-token generations per bad item) and spent DEADLINE_SECONDS, which the item-level retry does not. uer: _validate_item no longer collapses well-formed-but-empty into malformed; write_extraction marks such an item integrated, writes nothing, charges no attempt, and counts it in a new Tally.empty_extraction. Suite 1554 -> 1571 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped against live PG18; ruff clean. All four mutations caught (1/1/2/3 tests), and the two run()-level property tests assert the acceptance criterion (never re-offered) through the real integration SELECT rather than restating integrated_at, with a presence sibling proving a malformed row still comes back. NOT COMMITTED: awaiting approval per the conservative profile.

title: Reconcile the two memory corpora and correct CLAUDE.md's override rationale
description: Found 2026-09-04. This repo has TWO memory corpora and only one is live. LIVE: ~/.claude/projects/G--pythonDev-news-brief/memory/ - the auto-memory system reads and writes here and its MEMORY.md is what loads into context. ORPHANED: <repo>/.claude/memory/ - directory mtime 2026-08-29, 60 files against the live 67, and the shared files are far behind (env-var-needs-compose-passthrough.md is 2.7KB in the repo vs 9.7KB live, missing the whole 2026-09-02 phase-2 section). NOTHING HYDRATES IT: the repo's .claude/settings.json holds exactly one SessionStart hook, 'bd prime --stealth --hook-json'; the user-scope SessionStart hooks are serena-hooks activate, memory-index-nudge.sh and aegypt-wiki-context.sh. There is no hydrate-memory hook in either scope. WHY IT MATTERS: CLAUDE.md's REPOSITORY OVERRIDE rejects 'bd remember' on the stated rationale that '.claude/memory/ remains the durable memory corpus, hydrated by the hydrate-memory SessionStart hook, carried in git ... the file corpus already travels with the repo and needs nothing installed'. Every clause of that is currently false, so a cloud session or a second machine gets a clone carrying five-day-stale memories while the real corpus sits in a local directory absent from the clone. The DECISION may still be right; the REASON given for it is not evidence - textbook metadata-is-not-state.
design: Two coherent end states, and the current middle state is the only incoherent one because it documents a guarantee nothing provides. (A) Make it true: re-sync repo <- projects and build the hydrate hook. (B) Make it honest: delete the in-repo copy and rewrite the override to say memory is deliberately local-only, choosing bd/files on grounds that are actually true. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT on (A): the repo is PUBLIC and .claude/memory/ is already committed and public, so syncing is a PUBLISHING action over five-plus days of accumulated operational detail - review per file, never cp -r. That constraint is itself an argument for (B).
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md describes what actually runs, verified by reading both settings.json files rather than by reading CLAUDE.md. If the in-repo corpus survives, a hook demonstrably hydrates it and a live positive control proves the hook fires; if it does not, the directory is gone and the override's rationale no longer cites it.
close_reason: RESOLVED in ee9a1d0, option A per his call: 'memory should not be local only as I need it in remote sessions.' Corpora synced and verified byte-identical at 68 entries (diff -rq, exit 0; the same comparison listed 21 differences before). .claude/hooks/hydrate-memory.sh registered in .claude/settings.json INJECTS the committed MEMORY.md where the live corpus is absent and prints nothing where it is present; scripts/flush-memory.sh copies live->committed and stops without staging. CLAUDE.md gains a Memory section opening with the correction, so the acceptance criterion (CLAUDE.md describes what actually runs) is met by construction. KEY DESIGN DECISION, do not reverse: the hook does NOT copy files into the live corpus. The project key derives from cwd and all 26 keys on this machine are Windows drive paths, so the Linux form is UNVERIFIED -- a wrong key writes where nothing reads, silently, on the platform this serves. Measured: /home/user/... and /workspace/... derive no key, so detection fails to absent and the hook injects, meaning the unverifiable half fails safe. Copying would also overwrite a live corpus that is normally AHEAD. Verified in both directions: 0 bytes with the live corpus present, 22906 without; registered command works with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set and unset; flush detects new/changed/repo-only and --dry-run leaves corpora identical. PUBLISHING: all 21 delta files read in full. No credentials, keys, tokens or addresses. They do carry an operational map of the deploy host and a behavioural profile of him with verbatim quotes; he approved all 21 after review. 13 of the 21 were updates to files ALREADY in public git history, where withholding an update unpublishes nothing -- only the 8 new files were a real decision.

title: Size JOB_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES against real job_runs durations
description: 0q0.12 shipped the enforcement with a deliberately generous default of 240 minutes, chosen to clear the widest schedule grace (backup's 180) rather than measured against anything. That is safe but nearly useless: a collect that wedges still holds its row for four hours before anything reaps it. The measurement is one query, and the data already exists on the host: SELECT job_name, count(*), avg, percentile_cont(0.95), max over extract(epoch FROM finished_at - started_at) FROM job_runs WHERE both timestamps are non-null GROUP BY job_name. Set the row to something like 3x the observed p95 of the slowest job. This is a settings-row edit, NOT a deploy - which is why the cap was built as a knob. Do NOT lower it from a guess: the whole reason 0q0.12 sat open through Epic 7 is that a cap below a legitimate collect kills working runs, which is worse than the wedged child it prevents.
acceptance_criteria: JOB_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES is set from observed p95/max durations rather than from the schedule-grace floor, and the durations it was derived from are written into this issue so the next revision has a baseline to compare against.

title: The compose anchor declares NEWSBRIEF_CAPTURE_ENABLED but the knob's key is CAPTURE_ENABLED
description: docker-compose.yml:137 passes through NEWSBRIEF_CAPTURE_ENABLED. common.py:264 declares Knob(bool, False) with no env=, so Knob.key() returns the bare name and import_settings_from_env reads os.environ.get('CAPTURE_ENABLED'). The prefixed variable is therefore dead: it crosses the container boundary and nothing ever looks it up. Siblings confirm the convention - ENRICHMENT_ENABLED, BRIEF_MEMORY_ENABLED and CLAIM_VERIFY_ENABLED are unprefixed on both sides; NEWSBRIEF_RETENTION_DAYS is prefixed on both because its knob declares env=. Note the second, independent reason it stayed off: the importer only runs while settings is empty, so on an established host NO environment change can move a knob - direct SQL on the row is the only path. THIRD variant of this bug class: first the knob never reached the container, then the anchor line was missing, now the anchor line names a variable no code reads. Each layer was verified alone; the join between them never was.
acceptance_criteria: The anchor and common.KNOBS agree on capture's variable name, and a test derives the expected anchor names from KNOBS so a future knob cannot be declared under a name nothing reads. Existing test_config.py coverage cannot catch this: it exercises the importer with fabricated knobs (PG_A_ENABLED, PG_A_STAKE) and never reads the real docker-compose.yml.

title: Capture has no alerting path: spec 10's monitor integration was never built
description: The continuous-capture spec section 10 states as fact that 'the existing hourly monitor job raises capture health only on anomaly - failed feeds above a threshold, or zero new items across several consecutive passes'. That was never built. mode_monitor contains no reference to capture. The plan's own self-review claimed it was filed as a follow-up; it was not - Task 7 filed only news-brief-uh0 (retention). So capture currently writes capture_runs/feed_polls rows that nobody reads and nothing alerts on, and a capture that silently degrades (half the feeds 403ing) is invisible until someone queries the tables by hand. Deliberately kept out of b42.1 because the alerting threshold is unmeasured and guessing one puts an invented number on the critical path - but it must be tracked rather than assumed done. Depends on b42.2 having enough data to set the threshold empirically.
acceptance_criteria: mode_monitor reads capture_runs/feed_polls and raises on a threshold derived from observed data, not a guessed one. A capture where every feed fails produces exactly one alert, not 48.
notes: PARTIALLY DISCHARGED 2026-09-03 by news-brief-a9q, and deliberately not closed. mode_monitor now reads capture_runs and raises on the two conditions that need NO measured threshold: stale (no capture_runs row within STALE_AFTER_INTERVALS x the interval read from scheduler.SCHEDULES) and crashed (finished_at NULL on a run a later run has overtaken, which needs no timing constant at all - a successor proves the pass can never finish). Dedupe is a runtime_state key holding the episode, so a stopped capture alerts once and not once an hour; the acceptance criterion's 'exactly one alert, not 48' is covered by tests, including the positive control that a SECOND outage after a recovery alerts again. STILL OPEN and still blocked on b42.2: the QUALITY half - feeds-failed rate and items-new drought - which is what actually needs a number derived from observed data. /capture now renders those numbers without judging them, which is the evidence b42.2 will use.
close_reason: Quality half built: capture.failing_feeds (per-feed persistence, reusing STALE_AFTER_INTERVALS) and capture.item_drought (self-calibrating against 7 days of history), both on the (episode_key, message) contract with independent dedupe keys, wired into mode_monitor. 11 tests, 4 pre-registered mutations each failing exactly one.

title: Tests that pin 'the latest migration' silently defang 0006's negative control
description: Found twice during bqa.10. Adding migration 0007 broke two tests that hardcoded 0006 as newest, and one of them was the NEGATIVE CONTROL for the rollback test (test_the_rollback_assertion_can_actually_fail). db.run_migrations(direction='down') with no steps reverts only the NEWEST migration, so once 0007 sat on top the control reverted 0007 instead of the stripped 0006 down file, and the function it asserts survives survived for the wrong reason. It kept PASSING while testing nothing. Fixed for now with steps=2, which re-breaks on migration 0008. The same shape hit the boot-importer set in test_supervisor.py. Generalise both away from a literal count/list: derive the step count or assert on named versions.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a new migration requires no edit to test_kb_schema.py's rollback tests, and the negative control still fails when DROP FUNCTION is restored.
notes: REOPENED 2026-09-05: the sweep was INCOMPLETE and migration 0009 proved it. tests/test_capture_schema.py:119 calls db.run_migrations(conn, direction='down') with NO steps= at all, assuming 0008 is the stack top; adding 0009 made the bare call revert 0009 and 0008's three tables survived. It failed loudly rather than going vacuous, so it is a milder instance than the negative control -- but it is the same defect and the bead's title is about the CLASS, not about the two files named in the acceptance criterion. WHY THE SWEEP MISSED IT, which is the reusable part: I grepped for 'steps=' and fixed the three tests that carried an explicit count. A bare direction='down' has no steps= to match, so the pattern could not see the remaining instance -- pattern-cannot-match-the-shape, from my own probe-failures list, applied to my own fix. The correct probe was grep for direction=.down. across tests/, which returns all instances regardless of whether a count is present. Note tests/test_db.py:124 also uses a bare down call and is CORRECT: it monkeypatches MIGRATIONS_DIR to a temp dir with a throwaway migration, so it tests runner semantics rather than a real stack. Fix in flight as part of bqa.4b Task 1.
close_reason:
Resolved and now proven by a live event. Re-probed with the pattern that actually matches the shape -- grep 'direction=.down.' rather than grep 'steps=', since a bare down-call has no steps= to match, which is why the original sweep missed tests/test_capture_schema.py:119 and the issue had to be reopened.

Current state: test_capture_schema, test_claim_store, test_comprehension_schema and test_kb_schema (x2) all derive their step count via conftest.steps_back_through. The three remaining bare down-calls in test_db.py are CORRECT and must stay: they use the two_migrations fixture, which monkeypatches db.MIGRATIONS_DIR to a tmp_path holding a synthetic two-migration stack, so they test runner semantics rather than the real stack.

The proof is migration 0010 (sampled_at), added tonight during the comprehension-pipeline build: it landed on top of the stack and NOT ONE rollback test needed touching, because every count is derived. The only edit required anywhere was adding the migration's NAME to a hardcoded list in tests/test_db.py -- a different hazard, and one worth remembering separately: a hand-maintained list of migration names is invisible to probes that grep for len(), getsource or read_text.

title: /run <job>: manual on-demand runs via a queued row the supervisor claims
description: The commands daemon is a CHILD of the supervisor and cannot spawn a job itself, which is why migration 0001 carries trigger='manual' and status='queued' from the start. /run <job> validates against scheduler.SCHEDULES, INSERTs a queued row with scheduled_for NULL (so it cannot consume a scheduled fire time - latest_scheduled_for is max(scheduled_for) and ignores NULLs), and acks. The supervisor tick claims queued rows after _due_jobs so a manual request never starves a scheduled one, using the same claim-before-spawn ordering and the same spawn-failure close. A job already running leaves the row queued until the child exits. A queued row older than MANUAL_QUEUE_TTL is closed as missed with an alert rather than claimed, so a request made while jobs_enabled=False or during a long collect cannot fire hours later as a surprise. Collisions resolve through the existing advisory lock: the child exits EX_ALREADY_RUNNING and _closing_status already records that as missed. Split out of 0q0.9 (decided 2026-09-01): 0q0.9 is the read-only /jobs view, this is the write path.

Adds scheduler.next_fire, db.latest_runs/enqueue_manual/queued_runs/claim_queued, migration 0002 (job_runs.created_at, exercised down+up live). title: Backup job: pg_dump on the supervisor schedule, with an exercised restore

Success criterion 10 requires that a dump actually RESTORES into an empty database and the application starts against it: an unexercised backup is a belief, not a property, so the restore must be run once and the result recorded. Note the current JSON state has no backup at all beyond whatever the host does to the share, so this is a net gain either way. Depends on the supervisor scheduler existing.

Dockerfile installs postgresql-client-18 from PGDG: Debian trixie ships client 17 and pg_dump refuses to dump a newer server, so the Debian package would fail nightly and silently. backup.version_refusal compares client vs server major at runtime and alerts. RESTORE EXERCISED (criterion 10): real backup mode in the real image wrote a 9650-byte dump (pg_dump 18.6 pgdg13+2), pg_restore into a second EMPTY database owned by a different role, all 4 seeded rows restored in order, migration runner reports schema current. title: Job interlock: lock plus trigger/status, enforced in the mode dispatch
description: Every entry path to a job - the supervisor, docker compose run, and any future /run command - acquires a lock keyed on job_name and writes its job_runs row. Enforced in the mode dispatch, NOT in the supervisor, because a guard in the supervisor is exactly what the one caller bypassing the supervisor evades. Use pg_advisory_lock on a hash of the name so a killed child cannot strand it. Without this the sanctioned debug path (docker compose run --rm newsbrief collect) resurrects the double-collect this whole spec exists to prevent - the existing file_lock guards BOOK_FILE and STATE_FILE spans, never a mode. title: Trivy scan runs AFTER the image is pushed, so it alarms rather than gates
description:
Discovered 2026-08-31 while fixing CVE-2026-14456. In .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml the 'Build and push' step sets push: true and runs BEFORE 'Scan image for vulnerabilities'. On run 33396669659 the scan failed the run while the vulnerable image had already been published to ghcr.io as :latest and :sha-31bb170. So the gate marks the run red but does not stop a vulnerable image reaching the registry, and :latest - which the deploy tracks - is already overwritten by the time the scan speaks. The failing run is an alarm, not a gate, and it currently reads as a gate.

FIX SHAPE: build without pushing (push: false, load: true), scan the local image, then push in a second build step that hits the gha cache. Costs a second step and constrains to a single platform for load, which is fine here - the image is linux/amd64 only. ALTERNATIVE if that is judged too invasive: leave the ordering and make the docs/comment say plainly that the scan is post-publication, so nobody reads a red run as 'nothing shipped'.

NOT urgent: the scan does fail the run loudly, and this repo deploys by pulling a tag rather than automatically on green. Deliberately NOT bundled into the 2026-08-31 deploy - restructuring the publish path during an in-progress deploy is how you lose both.
notes: FIX COMMITTED b40c12d, NOT YET VERIFIED. docker-publish.yml now runs Build for scanning (push:false, load:true, tags newsbrief:scan) -> Scan -> Build and push (cache-from gha). The Lowercase image ref step is retired: it existed only because trivy got the raw cased github.repository. YAML parses and the step order was confirmed programmatically, but the behaviour this changes happens only on GitHub -- a local run cannot exercise it. KEEP OPEN until the first push to main shows the workflow green with the scan step preceding the push, and specifically confirm the second build is a cache HIT rather than a rebuild (if it rebuilds, the pushed layers are not provably the scanned ones and the gate is weaker than it reads).
close_reason: Verified on live run 34256471788: steps execute Build for scanning (push:false, load:true) -> Scan (trivy exit-code 1, CRITICAL/HIGH, ignore-unfixed) -> Build and push, with no if:always() on the push. A failing scan now stops the image reaching ghcr.io instead of announcing it afterwards.

title: Re-extract items integrated under the old integration schema
description:
bqa.16 changed the emit_extraction tool schema (anyOf branches on entities and events) WITHOUT bumping INTEGRATE_PROMPT_VERSION, deliberately. Items that FAILED validation have integrated_at NULL and pick up the new schema with no bump, so the fix reaches everything that was actually broken. The bump was withheld for two reasons, both time-limited:
